risks.description: A view billed as read-only silently performs a write (creates an effect grant, a claim row, or POSTs to the TMS) — the single most consequential failure for a write-fencing freight teammate.
risks.basis: AC 'the view performs no write of any kind' (weight 3, PENDING); effect_grants is the canonical single-commitment ledger per schema.py.

risks.description: A search that matches nothing renders a blank/empty result instead of explicitly saying no shipments matched, leaving the operator unsure whether the record is missing or the search broke.
risks.basis: AC 'a filter with no matches says so rather than showing nothing' (weight 2, PENDING).

risks.description: Search by an existing reference fails to return the matching shipment (wrong query, off-by-one param name, tenant mis-scoping), so the primary read is unreliable.
risks.basis: AC 'a search by reference returns the matching shipment' (weight 3, PENDING).

risks.description: Malformed or hostile search input (SQL metacharacters, over-long strings) crashes the endpoint (500) or, worse, injects into the read query and mutates state.
risks.basis: AC3 read-only invariant plus general query-construction risk on a new user-facing search surface.

risks.description: Adding the view regresses existing write-fence / tenant-first invariants that the canonical suite guards.
risks.basis: U-RO-3 adds a new surface into a codebase whose identity is a governed write fence; full canonical suite is the guard.

risks.description: The view leaks another tenant's shipments, since every canonical table is tenant-first but the AC set is silent on scoping for this new read surface.
risks.basis: schema.py enforces tenant-first PKs everywhere; the U-RO-3 AC set does not name tenant scoping — a gap, not a promise.

scenarios.title: No write of any kind after a reference search
scenarios.purpose: Prove the read-only view records no effect and claims no action after being exercised.
scenarios.rationale: The weight-3 load-bearing AC is that the view writes nothing; the canonical effect ledger and claim tables are exactly where an accidental write would land.
scenarios.generating_risk: A view claimed read-only silently creates an effect grant or claim row.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: the view performs no write of any kind
scenarios.isolation_note: Issues only GET reads; asserts absolute-zero on write-commitment tables, so it cannot contaminate later scenarios and needs no cleanup.

scenarios.title: Search by an existing reference returns that shipment
scenarios.purpose: Confirm a reference search surfaces the matching shipment and echoes its reference.
scenarios.rationale: The primary promised behaviour: a correct search for a seeded reference returns that shipment, whose reference must appear in the response.
scenarios.generating_risk: Search returns nothing or the wrong record for a reference that exists.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: a search by reference returns the matching shipment
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only GET; no state mutated, no cleanup required.

scenarios.title: Empty-result search says so rather than showing nothing
scenarios.purpose: Confirm a no-match search returns an explicit non-error response, not a blank/crash.
scenarios.rationale: AC2 requires an explicit 'no matches' answer; at minimum a correct product returns 200 with no traceback for an impossible reference.
scenarios.generating_risk: A no-match search renders blank or 500s, leaving the operator unsure if the record is missing or the view broke.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: a filter with no matches says so rather than showing nothing
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only GET; no mutation, no cleanup.

scenarios.title: Malformed search input does not crash or write
scenarios.purpose: Confirm special-character input is handled as a query, not a 500 and not a mutation.
scenarios.rationale: A new user-facing search box invites hostile/odd input; it must degrade gracefully and stay read-only.
scenarios.generating_risk: SQL metacharacters or over-long input crash the endpoint or reach the query layer and mutate state.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: the view performs no write of any kind
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only GET with hostile input; asserts write tables stay empty, so nothing carries over.

scenarios.title: Repeating the same search accumulates no state
scenarios.purpose: Confirm re-running an identical read is naturally idempotent and writes nothing.
scenarios.rationale: A read repeated by an operator (refresh, retry) must not accumulate rows in any write table.
scenarios.generating_risk: Each search invocation quietly appends a claim/telemetry write, so repeated reads grow state.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: the view performs no write of any kind
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only GETs repeated; asserts write-commitment tables remain empty, no cleanup needed.

scenarios.title: Canonical suite still passes with the new view
scenarios.purpose: Guard that adding the read-only view did not regress the write-fence / tenant-first invariants.
scenarios.rationale: The product's identity is a governed write fence; the canonical suite is the standing guard that a new surface didn't weaken it.
scenarios.generating_risk: The new view introduces an import or path change that regresses effect-ledger or tenancy invariants.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-RO-3: the view performs no write of any kind
scenarios.isolation_note: pytest builds its own temp databases; it does not touch the driver_probe workspace, so it is isolated by construction.

assumptions: The read-only shipment view is served by the loopback app at http://127.0.0.1:8001 as an HTTP GET surface (the prompt provisions a loopback app URL specifically for request paths); its exact route is assumed to be /shipments with a `reference` query parameter.

The app on 8001 is backed by data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 (the only approved sqlite3 target), and that DB has the canonical schema created at startup so effect_grants / operation_action_claims / delivery_action_claims exist and start empty for the run.
Shipment/load reference '560003' is seeded and resolvable (it recurs as a load/search reference across eval/tests/test_operator_agent.py); 'ZZ-NO-SUCH-REF-9999' resolves to nothing.
'No write of any kind' is verified as zero rows in the canonical write-commitment tables (effect_grants and the action-claim tables); read-only telemetry, if any, is not treated as a business write.
unresolved_questions: What is the actual surface and route of the read-only view (HTTP path + param names, CLI, or Slack read)? I could not locate an implementation of U-RO-3 in src/; every request-based scenario assumes GET /shipments?reference= and will spuriously fail if the real contract differs.

What exact text does the view emit for a no-match search? AC2 requires it to 'say so', but I could not find the copy string, so S3 can only assert 200-with-no-error, not the presence of the specific 'no shipments matched' message. Provide the literal string to strengthen the oracle.
What are the real seeded shipment references and their fields in the run's dataset? Without them the happy-path echo assertion (S2) is a guess ('560003').

Is the search meant to read the workflow DB, the mock TMS, or both? If shipments live in the mock TMS, a 'no write' check must also confirm no TMS mutation, which no approved command can currently inspect.

Should this view be tenant-scoped? Every canonical table is tenant-first, but the U-RO-3 AC set is silent on cross-tenant read isolation — this looks like a real gap (R6) that should be an explicit acceptance criterion rather than left inferred.
